title: A Poem About Being Witnessed, Not Rescued | Plea of a Bruised Soul
description:
There's a version of comfort that does more harm than silence. It rushes in, reframes, offers silver linings before the wound has finished bleeding — and the person on the receiving end learns to stop saying how they really feel.

This poem came from that place. Not from the pain itself, but from the loneliness of having your pain redirected by someone who genuinely cares.

"Plea of a Bruised Soul" is a plea not for rescue — but for witness. For someone to sit in the room where the ceiling has caved and not look away.

In this video I read the full poem and share two personal reflections: a moment when well-meaning comfort left me feeling more alone, and a time I was the one doing the over-advising — and what I'd do differently.
